name: Bupivacaine hydrochloride in dextrose

overview.class: Hyperbaric spinal local anesthetic; amide type
overview.mechanism: Bupivacaine blocks nerve-impulse conduction; dextrose changes solution baricity.
uses: Spinal/subarachnoid anesthesia. Product concentration, baricity, route and local insert must match the planned procedure.

usual_adult_dose.dose: No single numerical regimen is assigned across these Philippine products. The US comparator is 7.5 mg/mL with 82.5 mg/mL dextrose, whereas these registry records generally describe 5 mg/mL preparations; US milliliter schedules are not transferred [[USSPINAL,PHREG]]

contraindications: US spinal-label reference: Bier block; septicemia; severe hemorrhage, severe hypotension or shock; clinically significant arrhythmias such as complete heart block; amide-local-anesthetic/component hypersensitivity; local infection at lumbar-puncture site [[USSPINAL]]

common: US spinal-label reference: hypotension; hypoventilation from high motor block [[USSPINAL]]
serious: Systemic CNS/cardiovascular toxicity, respiratory arrest, methemoglobinemia [[USSPINAL]]

monitoring: US spinal-label reference: cardiovascular/respiratory vital signs and consciousness; experienced personnel and immediate oxygen/resuscitation resources [[USSPINAL]]

evidence.title: Product identity, kidney precautions and baricity evidence
evidence.intro: US label precautions are explicitly a comparator reference; they do not establish Philippine product equivalence or approved dosing.

rows.design: Product-data review; exact records listed in the products table.
rows.intervention: The cached Philippine registry groups 14 products here. Most state 5 mg/mL (0.5%) bupivacaine for spinal/intrathecal injection, frequently with 80 mg/mL dextrose. Rovacaine DRP-8310 instead lists 72.73 mg/mL (7%) dextrose; Genvacaine DRP-11010-01 has an ambiguous strength string. Do not assume one identical formulation across this heading.
rows.findings: The product heading alone is insufficient to establish concentration or interchangeability.
rows.limitations: Registration data are not a substitute for the current product insert; no numerical local regimen has been inferred.

rows.findings: Renal impairment may increase adverse-reaction risk and affects dose selection; only 6% is excreted unchanged.
rows.limitations: No CKD-band, HD, PD or CRRT regimen is established here. This spinal formulation is not an epidural/infiltration product.

rows.design: Double-blind study; 57 patients; spinal hyperbaric bupivacaine.
rows.intervention: 0.5% or 0.75% bupivacaine in 8% dextrose at varying volumes; research protocol.
rows.findings: Increasing volume prolonged duration with both concentrations. Greater cephalad spread occurred with increasing volume of 0.75%; the 3 mL 0.75% arm was stopped after seven patients because spread was excessive.
rows.limitations: Small historical study. Demonstrates concentration/volume sensitivity; does not validate a single volume, renal adjustment or equivalence across registered products.

draft_notes: US label is safety/background comparator only, not an exact-match label import. No dose/route/concentration transfer.
Registry strength strings preserved as data, not silently corrected. Product inserts linked in registry require separate verification for numerical local dosing.
Source verification uses existing delegated workflow. No new physician-personal-review claim; no inferred renal replacement dose.
